newsitem.title: CAMBODIA: Sihanouk threatens abdication over exiled prince.
newsitem.headline: Sihanouk threatens abdication over exiled prince.

text.p: King Norodom Sihanouk will abdicate immediately if a row over the planned return of his exiled half-brother leads to violence between Cambodia's two main parties, a letter released by the palace on Tuesday said.

Rumours have been circulating that former foreign minister Prince Norodom Sirivudh plans to return home for the April 13-15 Cambodian New Year with or without an amnesty for his alleged role in an assassination plot against co-Premier Hun Sen.
Sirivudh, who denies the charges, was placed under house arrest in late November 1995 and allowed to leave for exile in France on the intervention of his half-brother Sihanouk.
He was later sentenced to 10 years jail in absentia in a trial the international community branded a travesty.

But Sihanouk, in a letter dated April 7 to his son, First Prime Minister Prince Norodom Ranariddh, indicated that he was not prepared to risk a further deterioration in tense relations between the two premiers and their parties by pardoning Sirivudh.
Ranariddh recently urged the king to grant amnesty to Sirivudh, but Second Prime Minister Hun Sen has refused to ask the king to pardon Sirivudh.

"I am not in a position to make an enemy of Samdech Hun Sen, second prime minister of the royal Cambodian government, by granting an amnesty or royal pardon to HRH Samdech Krom Khun Norodom Sirivudh," Sihanouk wrote.
He said he had sacrificed much personal esteem in "saving the skin of Norodom Sirivudh" in 1995 and was not prepared to go through such humiliation ever again.

Sihanouk said it was up to the royalist FUNCINPEC party of Ranariddh and Hun Sen's Cambodian People's Party, which formed an uneasy coalition after U.N.-run general elections in 1993, to resolve the Sirivudh case in the interests of the country.

"As for myself, I am ready to abdicate immediately if this 'Norodom Sirivudh affair' is settled in violence," warned Sihanouk, who sparked a fresh political crisis in February by saying he was unhappy on the throne and thinking of quitting.

Hun Sen responded by saying local and general elections due in late 1997 and 1998 would be cancelled if the king stepped down and added that all members of the royal family should be barred from politics.
Analysts believe Hun Sen and his Cambodian People's Party fear Sihanouk would lead a royalist party to victory on the back of his grassroots support if he were to resign.
They believe he also fears the popularity and honest image of Sirivudh.

But some FUNCINPEC members told Reuters they believe Sirivudh should not return to Cambodia in the present climate, with tensions between the two parties at boiling point after the deadly March 30 grenade attack on a demonstration led by opposition leader and FUNCINPEC ally, Sam Rainsy.
